description: Recommended values for the `domain` field on control YAMLs. Soft enum: control authors may use a value not on this list, but `make domain-check` will warn so the choice is deliberate. Drift prevention without losing room for new categories.

canonical.description: Public reachability and broad-principal access. The single largest domain — covers anonymous read/write paths, wildcard policies, public IPs, internet-routable backplanes.
Posture / configuration discipline that does not directly create exposure. Includes compliance posture, organisational guardrails, SCP coverage, and account-level hygiene.
IAM principals, roles, trust policies, MFA, federation, blast radius.
Monitoring, alerting, alarm coverage, and detection-evasion concerns. Was previously also spelled `detect`; the canonical form is `detection`.
At-rest, in-transit, and key-management concerns. Was previously also spelled `encrypt` or `cryptography`; the canonical form is `encryption`.
Audit-trail completeness, retention, immutability, and integrity.
VPC, subnet, security group, peering, and routing posture distinct from exposure (which is the resulting reachability).
Backup, recovery, replication, multi-region availability. Subsumes the older `availability` value.
Resource lifecycle: orphans, stale snapshots, version retention, deletion protection.
Storage-specific posture not captured by exposure, encryption, or lifecycle (e.g. object lock, write-once, classification tagging).
Authorization mechanics distinct from identity (e.g. resource-based policy scoping, ACL semantics, presigned-URL hygiene).
Posture / cleanup signals with no specific MITRE attack-stage mapping. Used by orphan and stale-resource controls.
Secrets-management posture (Secrets Manager, Vault, SSM Parameter Store) — distinct from encryption-at-rest.
Operational capacity / quota concerns (per-region limits, scale ceilings).
